meanings.note: surprise or indignation: 'Ах ты, ...!' = why, you ...!

examples.text: Ах ты, жадина! А у тебя есть телефон?
examples.trans: Oh, you greedy thing! And have you got a phone?

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor

future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

заговорить.gloss: to start talking, begin to speak

meanings.en: to start talking, begin to speak, speak up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'говорить').

examples.text: Сейчас заговорит! В глаза мне смотри!
examples.trans: He will talk soon! Look me in the eyes!

meanings.note: A fact or a person.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

касаться.gloss: to concern, to apply to; to touch

meanings.en: to concern, to have to do with

+ genitive.

examples.text: Семьи это не касается. Это не по правилам!
examples.trans: Family is off-limits. That's against the rules!

meanings.note: professional associate (common gender, declined like feminine)

examples.text: Мой коллега помог мне с отчётом.
examples.trans: My colleague helped me with the report.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: That's it, Ninok. Now we have our own personal servant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; между собой = between yourselves/themselves

examples.trans: You two sort it out between yourselves here.

examples.text: Ну ладно, вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: All right, you two sort it out between yourselves here.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
молодой человек = young man (polite address)

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?

But legally you are nobody to her.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.

meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Informal.
Мой парень = my boyfriend.

examples.text: Всегда мечтала познакомиться с друзьями моего парня.
examples.trans: I've always dreamed of meeting my boyfriend's friends.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить').

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: + с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться').

examples.text: А как вы с ней познакомились?
examples.trans: And how did you meet her?

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

постоять.gloss: to stand for a while; to wait

meanings.note: Said to stop someone leaving. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять').

examples.trans: I'll stand here for a bit.

as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

рассказывай! = tell me (your news)!
